paragraphs: Ategrity Specialty Insurance Company Holdings is a specialty property and casualty insurance holding company dedicated exclusively to the excess and surplus ("E&S") market for small to medium-sized businesses ("SMBs") across the United States. Our underwriting operations are conducted through Ategrity Specialty Insurance Company, a Delaware-domiciled E&S insurer ("Ategrity Specialty").

We underwrite small and medium-sized commercial risks across selected industry verticals, including Retail, Real Estate, Hospitality, and Construction. The SMB segment of the E&S market is characterized by a high volume of smaller-premium policies, where distribution partners expect speed, clarity, and consistency in the underwriting process. Our operating model uses a technology-driven method to standardize, simplify, and where appropriate, automate these transactions, which we call productionized underwriting. This method incorporates micro-segmentation, centralized underwriting governance, and automated workflows to promote consistent, disciplined execution across a high-volume of E&S transactions.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, we generated $581.5 million in gross written premiums and reported a combined ratio of 88.2%. As of December 31, 2025, stockholders' equity was $614.3 million. Both Ategrity Specialty and Ategrity Specialty Insurance Limited ("Ategrity Limited") hold an "A-" (Excellent) (Outlook Positive) financial strength rating from A.M. Best.

We operate exclusively within the E&S market, a segment of the property and casualty insurance industry that provides coverage for risks that are typically unavailable in the admitted market. E&S carriers benefit from broad regulatory flexibility with respect to rate and form, which supports tailored product design and underwriting discipline.

Within the E&S market, we focus on SMB accounts. This segment is characterized by a high volume of smaller-premium policies and involves evaluating large numbers of submissions efficiently while applying consistent underwriting standards. Competition in this segment reflects responsiveness to distribution partners, pricing accuracy, and the ability to manage operational complexity at scale.

We operate a productionized underwriting model that combines technical underwriting with a centralized operating platform. We organize risks into micro-segments based on operational characteristics, geography, and exposure attributes, and use data analytics to develop risk models that inform our risk selection approach and pricing considerations.

We standardize key underwriting tasks, such as submission intake, risk classification, pricing and documentation, and automate them where appropriate. This structure supports efficient workflow across underwriting processes and promotes uniform execution.
We offer commercial property and casualty. All of our gross written premiums for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 were attributable to E&S products.
Our portfolio consists primarily of small- to medium-sized premium policies, including short-tail, lower-severity property exposures and shorter-tail, lower-limit, frequency-driven casualty risks.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, our gross written premiums were approximately 67.2% casualty and 32.8% property. Our business mix is diversified across products, policy sizes, and
industry verticals. Our property business is focused on insureds with limited catastrophe exposure, reflecting our emphasis on lower-severity risks.

We operate in 48 states and the District of Columbia. For the year ended December 31, 2025, five states accounted for 5% or more of gross written premiums: California (18.9%), Florida (16.1%), Texas (10.1%), New York (8.3%) and Georgia (5.4%).

We distribute our products exclusively through licensed surplus lines brokers and wholesale agents. Our distribution strategy is centered on providing a consistent and efficient experience to our partners across channels.

headings: Risks related to our business and industry

If we are unable to underwrite risks accurately and charge competitive yet profitable rates to our policyholders, our business, financial condition, and results of operations will be adversely affected.
Intense competition in the E&S market may limit our ability to maintain underwriting margins and growth.
We may be unable to obtain reinsurance coverage at reasonable prices or on terms that adequately protect us.
We are subject to reinsurance counterparty credit risk.
Our loss reserves may be inadequate to cover our actual losses, which could have an adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.
We rely on a select group of brokers, and such relationships may not continue.
Because our business depends on wholesale agents and brokers, we are exposed to certain risks arising out of our reliance on these distribution channels that could adversely affect our results.
Our failure to accurately pay claims in a timely manner and to monitor and detect fraud could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and prospects.
We may be unable to prevent, monitor, or detect fraudulent activity, including policy acquisitions or payments of claims that are fraudulent in nature.
Severe weather conditions and other catastrophes may result in an increase in the number and amount of claims filed against us.
If actual renewals of our existing contracts do not meet expectations, our written premiums in future years and our future results of operations and prospects could be adversely affected.
We may act based on inaccurate or incomplete information regarding the accounts we underwrite.
Our employees could take excessive risks, which could negatively affect our financial condition and business.
Changes in accounting practices and future pronouncements may materially affect our reported financial results.

Public attention to environmental, social, and governance initiatives may expose us to negative public perception, cause reputational harm, impose additional costs on our business, or impact our stock price.
Risks related to the market and economic conditions
Changes in interest rates and financial markets may adversely affect our investment income, book value and liquidity.
Global climate change may have an adverse effect on our financial results.
Risks related to the regulatory environment
Extensive and evolving insurance regulation and regulatory enforcement could restrict our operations, increase our costs and adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Failure to maintain our risk-based capital at the required levels could adversely affect our ability to maintain regulatory authority to conduct our business.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the factors discussed in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. References to past events are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether or not such factors have occurred in the past or their likelihood of occurring in the future. There may be additional risks and uncertainties of which we currently are unaware or currently believe to be immaterial. The occurrence of any of these risks could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, liquidity, results of operations, or prospects. In that event, the market price of our common stock could decline, and you could lose all or part of your investment.

In general, the premiums for our insurance policies are established at the time a policy is issued and, therefore, before all of our underlying costs are known. Like other insurance companies, we rely on estimates and assumptions in setting our premium rates. Establishing adequate premium rates is necessary, together with investment income, to generate sufficient revenue to offset losses, loss adjustment expenses, and other underwriting costs and to earn a profit. If we do not accurately assess the risks that we assume, we may not charge adequate premiums to cover our losses and expenses, which would adversely affect our results of operations and our profitability. Alternatively, we could set our premiums too high, which could reduce our competitiveness and lead to lower revenues.

Pricing involves the acquisition and analysis of historical loss data and the projection of future trends, loss costs and expenses, and inflation trends, among other factors, for each of our products in multiple risk tiers and many different markets. In order to accurately price our policies, we must:
•collect and properly analyze a substantial volume of data from our insureds; •develop, test, and apply appropriate actuarial projections and ratings formulas;
•closely monitor and timely recognize changes in trends; and
•project both frequency and severity of our insureds' losses with reasonable accuracy.

Loss ratio, expressed as a percentage, is the ratio of losses and loss adjustment expenses to net earned premiums.
Expense ratio, expressed as a percentage, is the ratio of underwriting, acquisition, and insurance expenses less fee income to net earned premiums.
Combined ratio is the sum of loss ratio and expense ratio. A combined ratio under 100% indicates an underwriting profit. A combined ratio over 100% indicates an underwriting loss.
Return on stockholders' equity is net income attributable to stockholders expressed as a percentage of average beginning and ending stockholders' equity during the period.

Our underwriting operations are conducted through Ategrity Specialty Insurance Company, a Delaware-domiciled E&S insurer.

We underwrite small and medium-sized commercial risks across selected industry verticals, including Retail, Real Estate, Hospitality, and Construction. The SMB segment of the E&S market is characterized by a high volume of smaller-premium policies, where distribution partners expect speed, clarity, and consistency in the underwriting process. Our operating model uses a technology-driven method to standardize, simplify, and automate these transactions, which we call productionized underwriting. This method incorporates micro-segmentation, centralized underwriting governance, and automated workflows to promote consistent, disciplined execution across a high-volume of E&S transactions.

We operate on a surplus lines basis in 48 states and the District of Columbia. For the year ended December 31, 2025, there were five states in which 5.0% or more of our gross written premiums were concentrated: California (18.9%), Florida (16.1%), Texas (10.1%), New York (8.3%), and Georgia (5.4%).
We operate our business in a single segment and as one reportable segment for purposes of assessing performance, making operating decisions and allocating decisions.
Gross written premiums are the amount received or to be received for insurance policies written or assumed by us during a specific period of time without reduction for policy acquisition costs,
reinsurance costs, or other deductions. The volume of our gross written premiums in any given period is generally influenced by:
•New business submissions; •Binding of new business submissions into policies; •Renewals of existing policies; and
•Average size and premium rate of new and existing policies.

Certain premiums and losses are ceded to other insurance and reinsurance companies under various excess of loss and quota-share reinsurance contracts. Ceded written premiums are the amount of gross written premiums ceded to reinsurers. We enter into reinsurance contracts to limit our exposure to potential large losses as well as to provide additional capacity for growth. Ceded written premiums are earned over the reinsurance contract period in proportion to the period of risk covered. The volume of our ceded written premiums is impacted by the level of our gross written premiums and any decision we make to increase or decrease retention levels.

Net earned premiums represent the earned portion of our net written premiums. Written premiums are earned on a pro rata basis over the terms of the policies, which are generally 12 months. The portion of premiums written applicable to the terms of the policies that have already elapsed is recorded as earned premiums.

Fee income includes policy fees charged to insureds and is recognized in earnings when the related premiums are written. These policy fees may be assessed as either a flat amount or a variable charge, depending on the specific policy type. The total amount of policy fee income is primarily impacted by the volume of our written policies.

Losses and loss adjustment expenses are a function of the amount and type of insurance contracts we write and the loss experience associated with the underlying coverage. In general, our losses and loss adjustment expenses are affected by:

paragraphs: Ategrity Specialty Insurance Company Holdings 為一家專注於美國小至中型企業（"SMBs"）之過度與盈餘（"E&S"）市場之專業財產與責任保險控股公司。本公司之承保業務由 Ategrity Specialty Insurance Company 進行，為一家設立於特拉華州之 E&S 保險公司（"Ategrity Specialty"）。
我們承保選定產業垂直領域之小至中型商業風險，包括零售、不動產、旅館與建設業。E&S 市場之 SMB 段落特徵為高數量之小保費保單，其中經銷夥伴期望承保流程具備速度、明確性與一致性。本公司營運模式採用以科技為導向之方法，以標準化、簡化並適當自動化這些交易，我們稱之為生產化承保。此方法包含微區段化、集中承保治理與自動化工作流程，以促進在高數量 E&S 交易中具有一致性與紀律性之執行。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們產生 581.5 百萬美元之毛承保 premiums，並報導綜合比率為 88.2%。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，股東權益為 614.3 百萬美元。Ategrity Specialty 與 Ategrity Specialty Insurance Limited（"Ategrity Limited"）均持有 A.M. Best 所給予之 "A-"（Excellent）（展望為正面）財務強度評級。
我們專注於 E&S 市場，為財產與責任保險產業之一個子市場，提供通常在正式市場中無法取得之風險覆蓋。E&S 保險業者因擁有廣泛之監管彈性，關於費率與形式，這支持個性化產品設計與承保紀律。
在 E&S 市場中，我們專注於 SMB 帳戶。此段落特徵為高數量之小保費保單，並涉及有效評估大量提交資料，同時應用一致之承保標準。此段落之競爭反映對經銷夥伴之回應速度、價格準確性與管理規模之運營複雜性之能力。
我們運作一生產化承保模式，結合技術性承保與集中運營平台。我們根據運營特徵、地理與風險屬性，將風險分為微區段，並使用數據分析來發展風險模型，以支援我們之風險選擇方法與定價考量。
我們標準化關鍵承保任務，例如提交資料接收、風險分類、定價與文件製作，並在適當情況下自動化這些任務。此結構支援在承保流程中之高效能工作流程，並促進一致執行。
我們提供商業財產與責任保險。我們於 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日之年度所產生之全部毛承保 premiums 均屬 E&S 產品。
本公司產品組合主要為中小型高階保單，包括短尾、低嚴重程度財產風險及短尾、低保額、高頻率意外風險。
截至2025年12月31日財年，本公司寫入 premiums 的毛額約為67.2%為意外風險，32.8%為財產風險。本公司業務組合跨產品類型、保單規模及產業垂直領域分散。
本公司財產風險業務著重於災害風險較低的被保險人，反映本公司對低嚴重程度風險的重視。
本公司營運範圍遍及48個州及華盛頓特區。截至2025年12月31日財年，五個州的寫入 premiums 佔比達5%或以上：加利福尼亞州（18.9%）、佛羅裏達州（16.1%）、德州（10.1%）、紐約州（8.3%）及喬治亞州（5.4%）。
本公司產品 exclusively 透過經許可的過剰線經紀人及總經銷商進行銷售。本公司銷售策略著重於為各通路的夥伴提供一致且高效的體驗。
本公司透過兩個主要通路進行產品行銷與銷售：

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與本年度10-K表報中所包含之合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。本討論與分析包含基於目前計畫、預期與信念之展望性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性。我們實際結果可能與這些展望性陳述所預期者有重大差異，原因可能包括「風險因素」中所列舉者，以及本年度10-K表報其他部分所列舉者。
Ategrity Specialty Insurance Company Holdings為專注於美國各州中小企業（"SMBs"）之過度與補充（"E&S"）市場之專業財產與意外保險控股公司。我們之承保作業透過Ategrity Specialty Insurance Company進行，為一家設立於德國的E&S保險公司。
我們承保各選定產業垂直領域之中小企業商業風險，包括零售、不動產、旅館與建設。E&S市場之SMB部門特徵為高數量之小額保費政策，其中經銷夥伴期待在承保流程中具備速度、清晰度與一致性。我們之營運模式使用以科技驅動之方法，以標準化、簡化與自動化這些交易，我們稱之為生產化承保。此方法包含微區分、集中承保治理與自動化工作流程，以促進在高數量之E&S交易中具有一致性與紀律性之執行。
我們在48個州及華盛頓特區以過度與補充（"surplus lines"）方式營運。截至2025年12月31日，有五個州之保費收入佔總寫入保費之5.0%或以上：加州（18.9%）、佛羅裏達州（16.1%）、德州（10.1%）、紐約州（8.3%）及喬治亞州（5.4%）。
我們營運業務於單一應報告分部進行，以評估績效、做營運決策及資源配置之目的。
寫入保費為指於特定期間內所收到或應收到之保險政策寫入或承擔之金額，不計減政策取得成本、再保險成本或其他扣除項。
任何特定期間內之寫入保費數量通常受以下因素影響：
•新業務申請；•新業務申請轉為保單；•現有保單之續保；以及
•新舊保單的平均規模與 premium rate。

某些 premium 和 loss 會根據各種 excess of loss 和 quota-share reinsurance 合約轉讓給其他保險與再保險公司。Ceded written premiums 是指轉讓給 reinsurers 的 gross written premiums 金額。我們會簽訂 reinsurance 合約以限制潛在大額 loss 的風險，並提供成長所需的額外 capacity。Ceded written premiums 會根據 reinsurance 合約期間，按風險覆蓋期間的比例確認收入。我們的 ceded written premiums 金額會受到 gross written premiums 金額以及我們是否提高或降低 retention 水準的影響。
Net earned premiums 代表我們 net written premiums 的已確認部分。Written premiums 會根據保單的期限，按比例確認收入，通常為 12 個月。已過期的保單期間所對應的 premiums 會記錄為 earned premiums。
Fee income 包含對被保險人收取的保單費用，並在相關 premiums 確認收入時確認。這些保單費用可能根據特定保單類型，以固定金額或變動費用的方式收取。總計的 policy fee income 金額主要受我們所寫保單數量的影響。
Losses and loss adjustment expenses 取決於我們所寫的保險合約種類與數量，以及基礎保障的 loss 經驗。總體而言，我們的 losses and loss adjustment expenses 會受到：
•特定類型保險合約相關的 claim 頻率。

headings: 與本公司業務及產業相關之風險
若我們無法準確評估風險並對保單持有人收取具競爭力且獲利的費率，將會對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
在E&S市場中激烈的競爭可能限制我們維持承保邊際及成長的能力。
我們可能無法以合理價格或足以保護我們的條款取得再保險覆蓋。
本公司面臨再保險交易對手信用風險。
我們的損失備抵可能不足以覆蓋實際損失，這可能會對本公司財務狀況、營運成果及現金流產生不利影響。
我們依賴少數的經紀商，這些關係可能無法持續。
由於本公司業務依賴於經銷商及經紀商，因此我們面臨某些因依賴這些通路而產生的風險，這些風險可能會對本公司營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司未能準確且及時支付聲請金額，並監測及偵測詐欺行為，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果及前景產生不利影響。
本公司可能無法防止、監測或偵測詐欺活動，包括涉及詐欺性質的保單取得或聲請金額支付。
嚴峻天氣狀況及其他災難事件，可能導致針對本公司的聲請案件數量及金額增加。
若本公司現有契約的實際續約情況未達預期，本公司未來年度的書面 premiums 及未來營運結果與前景可能受到不利影響。
本公司可能基於不正確或不完整資訊，對本公司承保的帳戶做出判斷。
本公司員工可能採取過度風險，可能對本公司財務狀況及業務產生負面影響。

paragraphs: 你應謹慎考量本年度報告表 10-K 所討論的各項因素。對於過往事件的提及僅為範例，並非完整列出或表示這些因素是否曾發生過或未來是否可能發生。我們可能尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未察覺或認為其重要性不高。若這些風險發生，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況、流動性、營運成果或前景造成重大且不利的影響。在此情況下，本公司普通股的市場價格可能會下跌，你可能會損失全部或部分投資。

通常，我們的保險保單 premiums 在保單發行時即已確定，因此在所有基礎成本皆明確之前。如同其他保險公司，我們在設定 premiums 時依賴估計與假設。設定適當的 premiums 是必要的，與投資收入結合，以產生足夠的收入來彌補損失、損失調整費用及其他承保成本，並賺取利潤。若我們未能準確評估所承擔的風險，我們可能無法收取足夠的 premiums 來覆蓋損失與費用，這將對我們的營運成果與獲利能力造成不利影響。另一方面，我們也可能設定過高的 premiums，這可能會降低我們的競爭力，並導致收入減少。
訂價涉及對歷史損失資料的取得與分析，以及對各產品在多個風險層級與許多不同市場的未來趨勢、損失成本與費用、以及通貨膨脹趨勢等各項因素的預測。為準確訂價我們的保單，我們必須：
•取得並正確分析來自被保險人的大量資料；•開發、測試並應用適當的精算預測與評分公式；
•密切監測並及時認知趨勢的變化；以及
•以合理準確的程度預測被保險人的損失頻率與嚴重程度。
